title: Slowly, little by little
hookLine: after the whole long teaching, Uddhava says it's too hard, and Krishna's answer is short and gentle
carry: every task offered, God seen in every being

cards: After all of it, the earth, the three paths, the beggar's song, the strands, Uddhava says something brave. He tells Krishna that the yoga he's described is hard for anyone who can't master the mind.
Hard, he says in effect, for people like us. Give us something a person can actually do. It's a student raising a hand at the end of a long lecture: I didn't get all that.
Krishna doesn't sigh or start over. His answer is short, and surprisingly gentle.

teach.h: DO ALL YOUR WORK FOR ME, SLOWLY.
teach.b: Krishna's answer, in paraphrase: do all your work for my sake, remembering me, slowly, little by little. That's it. No new technique.
The work stays the same: the cooking, the trading, the caring for children and parents. What changes is who it's for. Then he widens it.
See me in every being, he says, inside them and outside them, the way the sky is in everything.

teach.h: BOW EVEN WHERE OTHERS PASS BY.
teach.b: And then a line that asks a great deal: bow down to everyone, even to a dog, a donkey, a cow, even to the person your society pushes to the edges, and don't mind if your own people laugh at you.
The text names the creatures and people its own world looked past, and asks the devotee to bow there too. Notice that word, slowly. Not a crash course.
A lifetime of small handings-over, one task at a time. Then the dialogue ends. Krishna sends Uddhava to Badari, a hermitage in the mountains, to live what he has heard.
And Uddhava, who began by begging to go along, goes where he's sent instead.
This is the heart of bhakti in daily life, and it's why many Hindu homes offer the first of the cooking, or a day's work, to God before anything else.
The Uddhava Gita closes with a student walking away from his teacher, carrying the work. Tomorrow, the word for that kind of carrying.

how: Vaishnava Hindus speak of offering their daily work to Krishna, and the eleventh book of the Bhagavata, where Krishna tells Uddhava to do all his work for his sake and to see him in every being, is one of the texts they draw on.

o: work done for the one you love, little by little
a hard discipline only sages can master
a life given up to live in the mountains

games.q: the close of the Uddhava Gita — tap the pairs.
p: this yoga is too hard to do
do all your work for me, slowly
in every being, like the sky
where Uddhava is sent to live it

s: Krishna answers 'too hard' with a harder discipline
he gives something simpler: do all your work for his sake, slowly.
Uddhava ends the dialogue by going along with Krishna
he's sent to Badari, a hermitage in the mountains, and he goes.
Krishna asks the devotee to bow even to a dog or a donkey
seeing him in every being, the devotee bows to all, even where others pass by.

games.q: you're Uddhava. you've heard a long teaching, and you tell Krishna honestly it's too hard. what does he give you?
o: a stricter discipline to master the mind.
permission to give the whole thing up.
a simpler way: do all your work for him, slowly.
games.why: Krishna answers with something simple: do all your work for his sake, remembering him, little by little.

practice: Choose one small piece of work waiting for you and picture doing it start to finish at an unhurried pace, giving it away before you even begin.
If you pray, you can offer it to the One you pray to; if you don't, offer it to the person it will serve, and let the breath stay slow.

wordCard.voice: Karma. At the close of the Uddhava Gita: all your work, done for the one you love, slowly, little by little.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the name of Krishna's friend and questioner, for whom the Uddhava Gita is named.

carryVoice: Your line: every task offered, God seen in every being. Slowly, little by little, is how the text says it's done. I'll be here tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 11.29.1–3 (Uddhava says the yoga is hard for those who cannot master the mind)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.9 (do all actions for his sake, remembering him, little by little)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.12–16 (see him in all beings, within and without, like the sky; bow to all, even dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, disregarding the laughter of one's own people)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.40–47 (Krishna sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama; Uddhava departs)
